findings.title: Default-strategy deployments are created without the required rolling-updates feature
findings.body: createInitialDeployment() returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before enabling Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES. Both parameterized tests use the null/default strategy: testCacheMaxCount expects a rolling upgrade for the null case, and testImageChange also exercises the operator upgrade flow. The PR's own operator documentation states that the rolling-updates feature must be enabled or the operator will fail, and the CLI check now exits with FEATURE_DISABLED when it is not enabled. The null-strategy cases therefore either fail/recreate instead of rolling or are not actually testing the new feature-gated path. Enable rolling-updates for the default case as well, or explicitly document and adjust the expectations if the default path is exempt.

findings.title: New exit-code contract for disabled feature and recreate is not asserted
findings.body: This PR changes RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3 and introduces FEATURE_DISABLED=4, while the guide tells users to rely only on the check command's exit code. However testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the metadata subcommand and only asserts the stderr text; it does not assert exit code 4, and there is no equivalent disabled-feature test for the check subcommand. testWrongVersions likewise asserts messages but not exit code 3. A regression that swaps or breaks these codes would therefore pass the tests while breaking scripts and the operator that consume the numeric codes.

findings.title: Caution incorrectly implies all operator deployments fail without rolling-updates
findings.body: The added caution says that while in preview the rolling-updates feature must be enabled, otherwise the Keycloak Operator will fail. As written this is unconditional, but the same section documents '<not set>' as the default strategy that mimics Keycloak 26.1 or older behavior, which is a supported configuration that does not opt into the new update-strategy handling. Readers running the operator without spec.update.strategy will conclude they must enable a preview feature or their existing deployment will break. Scope the caution to deployments that actually use the update feature/strategy (for example when spec.update.strategy is set), mirroring whatever the operator really requires.
